scope: Measured material properties and explicit ideal assembly bounds; no assigned engineering credible interval.

sources.title: Thermophysical properties of advanced carbon materials for tokamak limiters
sources.authors: E. P. Roth, R. D. Watson, M. Moss, W. D. Drotning
sources.read_scope: Full report; printed pp. 10-14, Table I, Figures 12/14 and numerical appendix p.84 inspected. Figure12 and appendix p.84 visually checked.
sources.method: Laser-flash thermal diffusivity, measured density and common literature specific heat. All pyrolytic samples conduct parallel to deposition plane. Expansion correction omitted by authors.
sources.uncertainty: POCO calibration agreement within +/-5%; measured specific heats agreed within3% of common literature curve through700C. These are method checks, not an assigned total-conductivity confidence interval.

sources.read_scope: Full primary report; TableII and Figure5 visually checked.
sources.method: Guarded longitudinal heat flow on nearly isotropic AXF-5Q and H337 graphite.

sources.title: High Temperature Annealing of Irradiated Nuclear Grade Graphite
sources.authors: W. David Swank, David T. Rohrbaugh, David L. Cottle, William E. Windes
sources.read_scope: Full primary paper, thermal-diffusivity section and Fig13 discussion. Scratch filename is historical; authors are Swank etal, not Snead.
sources.finding: Thermal-diffusivity recovery starts near1000C; only lower-dose specimens fully recover by2380C. This is grade/dose-specific evidence, not a conductivity law for the proposed basal laminate.

roth_compression_annealed_basal.extraction: Numerical table transcribed and visually checked; decimal precision reproduces source, not uncertainty.

moore_unirradiated.location: TableII, PDF page14; original W/cmK multiplied by100

irradiated_comparison.scope: Approximate author summary across tested irradiated specimens; not a transferable damage multiplier for the catcher.

c_axis_evidence_gap.note: This review establishes high-temperature basal conductivity. The same grade's1000-1200K c-axis conductivity was not recovered from a full primary table, so it does not validate or change the archived surface-laminate k=4 assumption.
